Nxeon (VPS/game hosting business at /opt/nxeon, production Next.js app). Two real, confirmed bugs on the NxLabs mod-store pages to fix and deploy.

## Bug 1: No real pagination — hard 400-item cap

`lib/mods-catalog.ts`'s `listCatalogMods(family?)` (around line 174) does `take: CATALOG_LIST_CAP` where `CATALOG_LIST_CAP = 400` (line 40) — the file's own comment above it (lines 27-33) already documents this as a stopgap: "a follow-up should give StoreBrowser a real paginated/searched data source once a family regularly exceeds this." That threshold is now blown way past: the `minecraft` family alone has 32,251 rows (real Modrinth import, completed today) but customers can only ever see the top 400 by downloads/popularity — the other ~31,850 mods are permanently unreachable, with no page 2.

This is used from THREE call sites, all rendering through the same client component `components/mods/StoreBrowser.tsx`:
- `app/(marketing)/mods/page.tsx` (cross-game homepage, marketing)
- `app/(marketing)/mods/games/[family]/page.tsx` (per-family, marketing)
- `app/dashboard/nxlabs/page.tsx` (cross-game homepage, portal)
- `app/dashboard/nxlabs/games/[family]/page.tsx` (per-family, portal — check if this exists; if not, check how the portal reaches per-family browsing)

Fix: implement REAL server-side pagination. Read `StoreBrowser.tsx` in full first to understand how its existing client-side search/filter/sort works today (it currently runs client-side over the capped array). Design decision for you to make and document: either (a) keep client-side search/filter/sort but make it operate over a real paginated page of results with page-number controls (simplest, matches how the existing sort tabs work, acceptable since within one page filtering is still instant) plus a real total count shown, or (b) move search/filter/sort server-side too (bigger, more correct at 32k+ scale, real DB-level pagination with `skip`/`take` and `WHERE` clauses matching the current sort/filter options). Pick (a) unless you find the existing filter UX would be actively broken by only searching within the current page — if the search box is meant to search the WHOLE catalog (not just what's loaded), you need (b) for search specifically at minimum, even if you keep (a) for plain browsing. Look at what the search UI actually promises before deciding — don't guess, read the component's copy/placeholder text.

Use Next.js `searchParams` (`?page=2`) for the page state so it's a real shareable/back-button-friendly URL, standard for both marketing and portal (check `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx`-style patterns already in this repo for how other listing pages here do query-param-driven paging, if any exist — don't invent a new convention if one exists). Add real Prev/Next + page-number controls in the Nexion/marketing UI style already used elsewhere (check `components/nx/` for portal pagination primitives and `components/marketing/` for marketing ones before writing new UI from scratch). Show real "X–Y of N mods" copy, not fake page counts.

Raise or remove the 400 cap appropriately once real pagination exists (e.g. cap becomes a fixed page size like 24/48, not a total-catalog ceiling).

## Bug 2: Portal NxLabs homepage has no hero image

`app/(marketing)/mods/page.tsx` (marketing) correctly uses `PageHero` from `components/marketing/primitives.tsx` with `src="/nxlabs/hero-collage.png"` (the real board-provided mockup image, fixed earlier today after an invisible-image bug — see commit d6b9b55ff9 for that fix's context, the Reveal-gating issue).

`app/dashboard/nxlabs/page.tsx` (portal) uses `PageShell` from `components/nx/PageShell.tsx` with no hero/visual at all — just eyebrow/title/sub text. The user explicitly wants the hero image (the one from the board card, at `/opt/nxeon/.design-refs/nxlabs/portal-home.png` — that's the actual PORTAL mockup, distinct from `hero-collage.png` which is the marketing one) applied on the portal page too.

Read `/opt/nxeon/.design-refs/nxlabs/portal-home.png` (the real mockup) to see what the intended portal hero treatment looks like, and check whether `components/nx/PageShell.tsx` already supports a hero/visual slot (check other portal pages that might already have one, e.g. dashboard home `/dashboard/page.tsx` or similar) or whether one needs to be added. Match the actual Nexion portal design language (navy/violet/cyan, the existing sidebar/shell aesthetic) — do NOT just paste the marketing `PageHero` component into the portal, since portal pages don't share marketing's visual chrome (no public nav/footer, different content width, different card/surface conventions). If `PageShell` has no hero slot, add one in a way other portal pages could reuse (real utility, not this-page-only), matching the pattern of how other real page-level features got added to this shell previously (git log on `components/nx/PageShell.tsx` for context if useful).

## Process (mandatory, per this repo's discipline)
- Read the actual files listed above in full before changing anything — don't guess at current behavior.
- Never construct/print a raw psql/DATABASE_URL string. Any DB reads go through `db` from `lib/db` via a `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` script run with `npx tsx`, then delete the temp script when done.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean before considering this done.
- Take real Playwright screenshots (marketing /mods, portal /dashboard/nxlabs, and a per-family page with real page-2 navigation) before and after, comparing against `/opt/nxeon/.design-refs/nxlabs/portal-home.png` for the hero fix specifically.
- Build via `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh main` (NEVER build directly in /opt/nxeon — worktree/build-isolation rule), verify staging HTTP 200 at the exact new commit, verify the hero image and pagination controls actually render and work by curling/screenshotting staging, THEN `bash scripts/promote-production.sh`, and confirm production's `.next/BUILD_ID` actually changed plus a fresh `ActiveEnterTimestamp` on `nxeon-web`/`nxeon-worker`.
- Add a dated entry to `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` per this repo's required-docs-per-commit convention.
- Commit with a clear message; this repo auto-pushes on commit (confirm `git log origin/main` matches after).

Report back: what pagination approach you chose and why, confirmation of real page-2+ navigation working live (with actual URLs/counts), and confirmation the portal hero image renders live matching the mockup.

2	# Promote the currently deployed staging commit to production.
3	# Verifies staging is healthy, fast-forwards nothing (prod working tree IS the repo),
4	# then rebuilds + restarts production services.
5	set -euo pipefail
6	
7	STG_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon-staging rev-parse HEAD)

9	
10	echo "==> Staging is at:    $STG_COMMIT"
11	echo "==> Production is at: $PROD_COMMIT"
12	
13	if ! systemctl is-active -q nxeon-staging-web; then
14	  echo "Refusing to promote: staging web service is not running." >&2
15	  exit 1
16	fi
17	CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
18	if [ "$CODE" != "200" ]; then
19	  echo "Refusing to promote: staging returns HTTP $CODE." >&2
20	  exit 1
21	fi
22	
23	if [ "$STG_COMMIT" != "$PROD_COMMIT" ]; then
24	  echo "Note: production tree is at a different commit than staging."
25	  echo "Production deploys directly from /opt/nxeon's working tree (main)."
26	fi
27	
28	cd /opt/nxeon
29	echo "==> Installing dependencies (adds any new deps before build)"
30	# CRITICAL: without this, a commit that adds a new dependency (e.g. imapflow)
31	# builds against a stale node_modules and fails — which previously aborted the
32	# promote AFTER the old build was already gone. Always sync deps first.
33	npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3
34	# CRITICAL: this was previously `prisma generate` only — regenerates the
35	# CLIENT's types (fixes the build) but never touches the actual DATABASE.
36	# Staging and production are SEPARATE databases (nxeon_staging vs nxeon, same
37	# Postgres server, confirmed live) — deploy-staging.sh's own `db push` only
38	# ever applies to staging's DB, so a schema change promoted this way built
39	# and deployed fine while production's actual table never got the new
40	# column, silently breaking the FIRST thing that queried it post-deploy
41	# (found live 2026-09-02: worker/billing.ts's sweeps started throwing
42	# "column does not exist" immediately after a routine promote — no staging
43	# failure gave any warning, since staging's own db push had already
44	# succeeded there). `db push` both applies the schema AND regenerates the
45	# client, so this replaces the old generate-only step rather than adding a
46	# second one. Schema changes are rare enough that this always running
47	# unconditionally costs nothing when there's nothing new to push.
48	echo "==> Applying database schema"
49	npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss --schema=/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma 2>&1 | tail -4
50	echo "==> Building production"
51	npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

53	# always writes .next/BUILD_ID; if it's missing the build failed mid-way and the
54	# old in-memory process is still serving — abort rather than kill it.
55	if [ ! -s /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID ]; then
56	  echo "BUILD FAILED: .next/BUILD_ID missing — NOT restarting (old process left serving)." >&2
57	  exit 1
58	fi
59	# next.config sets output:"standalone"; the standalone server.js is what the
60	# systemd unit actually runs (not `next start` — see deploy-staging.sh's own
61	# comment on this same step for the 2026-09-10 incident). Its output does NOT
62	# include public/ or .next/static/ (Next's documented behavior) — refresh
63	# them every promote, same as staging, or new/changed static assets are
64	# missing from prod until the next promote happens to also touch this step.
65	echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
66	rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
67	cp -r public .next/standalone/public
68	cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
69	# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
70	# bundle since it reads .dat files off its own package path at runtime) — the
71	# standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace as JS-imported, so
72	# an externalized package's own non-JS data files are silently left behind.
73	# Found live 2026-09-10 on staging: this crashes EVERY request with an
74	# uncaught ENOENT the moment something runs the standalone server.js instead
75	# of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around geoip.lookup() does NOT
76	# help, the failure isn't confined to that call. Copy the real data/
77	# directory every promote, same reasoning as public/.next/static above. This
78	# has NOT yet bitten production because nxeon-web's systemd unit still runs
79	# `npm start` (next start) today, not server.js directly — but this fix must
80	# land before that switch happens, not after.
81	if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
82	  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
83	  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
84	fi
85	# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. .next needs to be writable by it
86	# (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable. .env is the one
87	# exception: systemd's EnvironmentFile= reads it as root (PID 1, pre-privilege
88	# drop) so the app's process env is fine either way, but Prisma's generated
89	# client ALSO opens .env directly at Client instantiation to resolve its own
90	# env() directives — that read happens as the actual 'nxeon' process user, so
91	# a root-owned .env throws EACCES there on every cold start (harmless once
92	# systemd's injected vars are already in process.env, but noisy, and a prior
93	# root-run edit to this file silently reverted the ownership fix below once
94	# already — confirmed live 2026-09-02). Keep .env nxeon-owned, not world- or
95	# group-readable. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
96	echo "==> Fixing .next/.env ownership for non-root web"
97	chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.next 2>/dev/null || true
98	chown nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true

103	# Drain in-flight provisions before bouncing the worker. Restarting the worker
104	# mid-provision used to interrupt a live VM build and (with a non-idempotent retry)
105	# strand the server in ERROR. The start step is now idempotent so this is
106	# belt-and-suspenders, but avoiding the interruption entirely is cleaner. Bounded
107	# wait (max ~4 min) so a deploy can never hang forever.
108	DBURL=$(grep -E '^DATABASE_URL=' /opt/nxeon/.env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"')

112	    [ "${ACTIVE:-0}" = "0" ] && break

116	fi

## NxLabs — real server-side pagination (32k+ mod families) + portal homepage hero (2026-09-19)

**The bug.** `lib/mods-catalog.ts`'s `listCatalogMods()` capped every query at `CATALOG_LIST_CAP = 400`
rows, ordered by featured/downloads/popularity — a documented stopgap since the file's own Phase 1
comment. `scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts`'s real bulk import landed 32,251 real `minecraft` rows
(verified live: `db.gameMod.count({ where: { active: true, upstreamOk: true, gameFamily: "minecraft" } })`
→ 32,251; 32,331 active/upstream mods total across all 5 families). Customers could only ever see the
top 400 by downloads — the other ~31,850 were permanently unreachable, with no page 2, on all four
StoreBrowser call sites (`app/(marketing)/mods/page.tsx`, `.../mods/games/[family]/page.tsx`,
`app/dashboard/nxlabs/page.tsx`, `.../nxlabs/games/[family]/page.tsx`).

**The fix.** `listCatalogMods`/`searchCatalogMods` are gone, replaced by
`queryCatalogMods({ family, category, q, sort, page, perPage })` — real DB-level pagination
(`skip`/`take` off a real `count()`), matching the existing `lib/pagination.ts` `paginate()` helper this
codebase already uses for `/blog` and the admin tables (extended with a new `buildHref()` for
building filter-preserving links). `CATALOG_PAGE_SIZE = 24` is now a page size, not a catalogue ceiling.
Chose full server-side search/sort/filter (option "b" of the two considered), not just server-side
paging with client-side search over one loaded page (option "a"): `StoreBrowser`'s own search
placeholder ("Search mods, plugins, and more…") promises to search the catalogue, not whatever page
happens to be loaded, and the family/category chips already advertised real DB-wide counts
(`listCatalogFamilies`'s groupBy) that a client-side filter over ~24 loaded rows could not actually
satisfy at this scale (a chip reading "1,842" could show 0 results). `StoreBrowser.tsx` is now a Server
Component — search is a native GET `<form>`, sort tabs/chips/pager are plain `<Link>`s carrying
`?q=&sort=&category=&page=` — no client JS required for the store to work at all (`QuickAddButton`
stays its own small Client Component). One honest, documented exception: "Top Rated" sort still
re-sorts by rating WITHIN each page rather than DB-wide, because avgRating has no cached column on
`GameMod` and Prisma's relation-`orderBy` only supports `_count` (not `_avg`) on to-many relations —
see the `ORDER_BY` comment in `lib/mods-catalog.ts`. Cross-game family chips now link to the real
`/mods/games/[family]` (or portal equivalent) pages instead of re-filtering in place, since those pages
already exist and are correctly paginated. Added `listCategoryCounts(family)` (real per-family groupBy,
replacing category counts derived from whichever page was loaded) and `totalDownloadsFor(family?)` (a
real `_sum` aggregate, replacing a `reduce()` over the same partial page) so the "X mods" / "Y total
downloads" stat rows stay accurate at every family size.

**Portal NxLabs homepage hero.** `app/dashboard/nxlabs/page.tsx` rendered through `PageShell` with no
`heroImage` at all, unlike its own sibling per-family page (`.../nxlabs/games/[family]/page.tsx`), which
already uses `PageShell`'s existing `heroImage` prop (a right-anchored illustration slot — see
`components/nx/PageShell.tsx`'s own doc comment). No shell change was needed: passed
`heroImage="/nxlabs/hero-collage.png"` (the same real board-provided art the marketing `/mods` page uses
via `PageHero`, fixed for visibility in the prior entry above) to the cross-game portal homepage, the
same way the per-family portal page already does with its own per-game hero art. Deliberately did not
port marketing's `PageHero` component itself into the portal — portal pages don't share marketing's

reuses the portal's own existing, already-proven hero mechanism instead.

working Prev/Next/page-number links; the portal NxLabs homepage renders the hero collage image.
